best_for: Minecraft players who mod their game and want a free, open-source launcher that installs and updates mods and modpacks from Modrinth, and who do not mind an ad unless they subscribe.
description:
Modrinth App is the desktop launcher for Modrinth, the site where thousands of Minecraft mods and modpacks are hosted. It is made by Modrinth and released under the GPL-3.0 license.

Because the app is tied to the website, the projects you follow there are a click away inside it. You can switch between your Minecraft skins without opening a browser, and reuse the same options and resource packs across every setup you play. If you run a server, you can share it with friends from the app; when they accept, they get a setup that your server keeps in step. Instances can sit in groups and carry their own custom icons.

points.title: Mods in one click
points.text: The launcher installs, updates and removes mods and modpacks from Modrinth, and lets you build and share your own packs. Each instance keeps its own mods and settings.

points.title: Brings your old setup
points.text: You can import existing instances from your previous launcher; the page shows GDLauncher and MultiMC among them.

points.title: Free and open source, with ads
points.text: The app is GPL-3.0 and free to download. It shows ads; Modrinth+ removes them for USD 4.99 per month, with 16% off on annual billing, and half of the fee goes to creators. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Still labeled beta
points.text: Modrinth offers the app as a beta. Its help center has articles for sign-in problems, crashes, broken Edge WebView2 installs on Windows and Java launcher errors.

points.title: Linux works with caveats
points.text: Modrinth notes known stability issues on Linux and has a help article on a laggy interface there. The Flatpak is published by Rinth, Inc., Modrinth's company, and Flathub marks it verified for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows installer is per-user, so no administrator rights are needed. The Windows listing keeps 145 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, and the Flatpak was at 0.23.1 when Windows and Mac were at 0.23.4.
